html:
Same-sex marriage became legal in Thailand on 23 January 2025, making it the first country in Southeast Asia to allow it. On the first day more than a thousand couples registered their marriages.

Thailand had long been seen as open toward gay and transgender people, but the law did not let them marry. After years of campaigning and several failed bills, the Marriage Equality Act was backed by the government of Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin and by most opposition parties. It passed the House by 400 votes to 10 in March 2024 and the Senate by 130 to 4 in June, and King Vajiralongkorn signed it in August.

The law changed the words "men and women" to "individuals" and gave same-sex couples the same rights to adopt, inherit and make medical decisions.

Thailand was the third place in Asia to allow such marriages, after Taiwan in 2019 and Nepal.
sum: Same-sex marriage became legal in Thailand on 23 January 2025, making it the first country in Southeast Asia to allow it. On the first day more than a thousand couples registered their marriages.
